correctness.rationale: For each zero-zero edge \(a_i b_j\) with \(i\ne j\), the neighborhood union is all vertices except \(a_j\) and \(b_i\), so the condition is exactly \(W-x_j-y_i\ge2\). Failure requires \(x_j+y_i\ge W-1\) and is impossible for \(W\ge6\). The proof exhausts the forced patterns for weights \(0\) through \(5\) and counts them exactly; direct exhaustive enumeration for \(n=3,4,5,6\) agrees with the complete polynomial and minimum-function classification.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-weight classification on a standard infinite regular bipartite family for a recently introduced NP-hard invariant. The defect-polynomial phenomenon is structural: relative to \(K_{n,n}\), deleting one perfect matching changes feasibility only through weight \(5\) while all labelings of weight at least \(6\) remain feasible. The result is substantially stronger than a scalar minimum and supplies a natural benchmark separating vertex–edge Roman \(\{2\}\) domination from the stronger vertexwise Roman \(\{2\}\) condition.
